Lithuanians speak Lithuanian (lietuvių kalba) as their primary and official language [d1][d6][d7]. It is an East Baltic language belonging to the Baltic branch of the Indo-European language family, native to about 85% of the Lithuanian population and spoken by approximately 96% [d1][d7]. Lithuanian is considered one of the oldest surviving Indo-European languages, retaining archaic features close to Proto-Indo-European, making it linguistically comparable to Sanskrit [d2][d9]. Beyond Lithuanian, minority communities and many Lithuanians also speak Russian, Polish, Belarusian, and English, with many Lithuanians being bilingual or even trilingual [d3][d5][d8].
